newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cen.bank denies changed money mkt policy.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cen.bank denies changed money mkt policy.

text.p: The National Bank of Belgium denied on Tuesday it was offering liquidity twice a day to the money market following last week's rise in Treasury bill yields.
"We have not changed our policy as far as (offering liquidity) once a day," a senior official at the central bank told Reuters.

One Belgian money market dealer said on Monday the central bank had been offering liquidity twice daily to the market since last Wednesday. This was the main reason yields moved lower on Monday, he said.
The central bank official said the amount of liquidity in the market was being closely monitored.
"We are assessing the situation each day now to see to what extent the degree of the squeeze (on liquidity) could be lessened," he said.

Yields on three month Treasury bills rose to 3.57 from 3.42 percent at last Tuesday's auction as a weeks long squeeze on money market liquidity, designed to bolster the Belgian franc, finally took its toll.
Treasury bill traders had previously warned such a move could take place because players were losing money financing positions because of the differential with money market rates.
Three month bills were yielding around 3.39/42 percent on Tuesday, unchanged on late Monday levels.
